title: Manufacture transplantable human kidneys from cells

concept.text: The innovation would be to grow and assemble cells into a transplantable human kidney that provides durable renal replacement at therapeutic human scale. The intended organ would contain enough working nephrons—the kidney’s filtering and processing units—connected to a blood supply and a system that collects and drains urine. It would support fluid, electrolyte and acid-base balance through coordinated filtration, tubular processing and excretion.

Concept synthesis: the defining achievement is integrated physiological replacement in a recipient. Producing more kidney organoids, improving their vascularization or showing that they filter an experimental tracer would establish useful components of that capability. A manufactured replacement kidney would additionally need sustained function, safe cell composition and a reproducible production process. The supplied study demonstrates progress toward this goal, rather than its completion.

significance.text: Conditional impact synthesis: reproducible manufacture of safe, functional kidneys could create a replacement-organ supply independent of kidneys procured from living or deceased human donors. The revolutionary change would be the ability to produce replacement organs through a controlled manufacturing process. Whether that capability materially reduced donor scarcity would depend on production capacity, organ durability, clinical eligibility, cost and access.

Patient-derived or otherwise compatible cells might also enable organs with a lower risk of rejection, but this remains a separate possibility. Manufacture from cells does not itself establish immune compatibility or freedom from immunosuppression. The supplied study used immunodeficient mice and provides no clinical rejection comparison, so its transplantation results cannot establish either benefit.

Impact synthesis: a dependable replacement-organ supply could change how kidney failure is treated, but the manufacturing analogy has limits. A living organ must develop, integrate with its recipient and maintain regulated function over time; increasing tissue output alone does not establish a useful transplant supply. Successful manufacture would also leave surgical delivery, recipient care and equitable deployment to be demonstrated.

missing_breakthrough.text: The central scientific gap illustrated by the supplied study is the transition from vascularized nephron tissue with a tracer-filtration signal to an integrated replacement organ. Its organoids lacked collecting ducts and could not drain urine. Connecting nephron output to a functional collection and drainage system is therefore a concrete unresolved requirement in this experimental preparation: filtration without an exit route does not establish sustained urinary excretion.

The reported vascular integration and filtration evidence also leave therapeutic scale and comprehensive maturation unresolved. A replacement organ would need sufficient functional nephron capacity, dependable blood flow and coordinated tubular handling to maintain the recipient’s internal balance. The study did not establish complete adult-organ maturity, physiological clearance sufficient for renal replacement or life-sustaining function.

Engineering synthesis: translating this concept into a repeatable therapy would require control over cell composition, tissue organization, organ-to-organ variability and long-term safety, together with a manufacturing process that reliably yields transplantable organs. These are proposed therapeutic requirements, rather than a checklist established by the supplied paper. Its stated future goal of implantable bioengineered kidneys manufactured to clinical quality does not demonstrate that these barriers have been overcome.

current_state.text: In a study published on February 2, 2026, Tekguc and colleagues reported human pluripotent-stem-cell-derived kidney organoids, vascularized tissue assembled into nephron sheets, and integration between human endothelial networks and host mouse vasculature after implantation. The work was a nonclinical laboratory study and involved no patients or human therapeutic testing.

The production work included a stirred-bioreactor differentiation protocol that generated SIX2-positive nephron progenitor cells from the H9 and BJFF.6 human pluripotent stem-cell lines within 7–8 days of induction. This is a reported interval for an early differentiation stage, not the time required to manufacture a mature transplantable kidney. It provides evidence for a scalable tissue-production route without establishing reproducible production of clinically functional whole organs.

Following implantation into immunodeficient NSG mice, imaging at 6–11 days and fixed-tissue analyses showed different distributions of 3 kDa and 500 kDa dextran tracers. Together with a diffusion-control experiment, the textual results supported the authors’ interpretation that the smaller tracer underwent glomerular filtration and subsequent tubular uptake or reabsorption, while the larger tracer remained excluded from tubules and the interstitial space. These complementary observations support evidence consistent with size-selective filtration; they do not establish a comprehensive physiological selectivity threshold or clinically sufficient clearance.

The organoids lacked collecting ducts and could not drain urine. Complete adult maturation, sustained renal replacement and human therapeutic function were not demonstrated. The reported short-term mouse observations therefore establish component-level progress, while the paper’s discussion of future implantable bioengineered kidneys for replacement therapy remains prospective.

Evidence scope: the supplied review assessed full main-article text available in HTML and PDF, but did not visually inspect the figures or movies. Supplementary PDF extraction omitted image content and included pages without extractable text, so it could not independently validate those images. These limitations constrain independent assessment of the reported visual evidence; they do not establish that the results are false.

Freshness limitation: the supplied material contains no bounded freshness-search record establishing field-wide status as of November 1, 2026. It supports the account of this February 2026 study, but cannot establish that this was the latest advance or that every other approach remained below the therapeutic target at that later date.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed clinical demonstration: independently manufactured kidneys would sustain recipients with kidney failure without dialysis over years, with measured filtration, fluid and electrolyte regulation, acid-base control and reliable urinary drainage. A convincing protocol would need to show that the manufactured graft provides the required replacement function, with predefined renal-function, safety and durability endpoints. Years of follow-up and dialysis independence are proposed operational goals here, not published consensus thresholds supplied by the source.
completion_criteria.label: Manufactured kidneys provide renal replacement without dialysis over years

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility demonstration: independent manufacturing teams would produce organs that repeatedly meet defined composition, structure, function and safety specifications across multiple batches, followed by reproducible transplantation outcomes. Testing should establish the range of cell sources, recipients and operating conditions under which the therapy works. Finite demonstrations would establish that tested breadth, rather than universal suitability for every patient or manufacturing condition.
completion_criteria.label: Independent teams meet manufacturing specifications and reproduce transplantation outcomes

completion_criteria.text: Proposed practical demonstration: production capacity, failure rates, cost and delivery requirements would support a credible path to materially reducing donor scarcity. Any claim of reduced rejection or freedom from immunosuppression would require its own immune-compatibility and clinical evidence. Functional success in a limited clinical setting would establish an important milestone, while broad supply and access would require additional demonstration.
completion_criteria.label: Practical production supports a credible path to reducing donor scarcity

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: NEP-01, “Regrow functional nephrons inside an adult human kidney,” overlaps in nephron generation and maturation, but aims to restore tissue within an existing kidney. NEP-02, “Rebuild function in scarred kidneys by reversing established fibrosis,” aims to recover function in a damaged native organ. NEP-03 instead targets manufacture of a separate transplantable replacement; progress in regeneration or fibrosis reversal would not by itself demonstrate that capability.

Roster-based synthesis: NEP-04, “A durable, implantable artificial kidney,” shares the objective of sustained renal replacement through an implanted system, while NEP-03 specifies a human kidney manufactured from cells. NEP-05, “Kidney replacement that is portable and affordable at global scale,” emphasizes delivery, affordability and reach. Manufactured kidneys could contribute to that goal if practical constraints were solved, but successful organ manufacture would not itself establish global affordability or access.

Roster-based synthesis: NEP-06, “An effectively unlimited supply of durable animal-donor kidneys,” addresses organ scarcity through animal donors rather than cell manufacture. NEP-07, “Reliably induce donor-specific tolerance in kidney recipients,” addresses the recipient’s immune response. Tolerance could complement manufactured-organ transplantation, but it remains a distinct capability and cannot be inferred from production of kidney tissue.

Roster-based synthesis: NEP-08, “A root-cause, durable treatment for ADPKD,” NEP-09, “Durable reversal of diabetic kidney disease,” and NEP-10, “Broad prevention of severe acute kidney injury,” target causes or pathways of native-kidney damage. Their success could reduce the need for replacement kidneys. NEP-03 addresses replacement after sufficient function has been lost and would not, by itself, demonstrate treatment of those underlying diseases or prevention of injury.

change_log.change: Preserved NEP-03 and its original title while defining the target as integrated, durable renal replacement at therapeutic human scale.
change_log.reason: Keeps the concept identity and distinguishes a transplantable replacement kidney from organoid production or a tracer assay.

change_log.change: Bound statements about unmet capability to the supplied study and separated them from unresolved field-wide status in November 2026.
change_log.reason: The February 2026 paper and empty freshness record cannot establish the status of every approach at the later date.

change_log.change: Expanded the experimental account to include nephron sheets, vascular integration, immunodeficient NSG hosts, the 6–11-day observation interval, 3 and 500 kDa tracers, fixed-tissue analyses and the diffusion control.
change_log.reason: Preserves the review’s scientific reasoning for the filtration interpretation and its experimental boundaries.

change_log.change: Qualified filtration as evidence consistent with size-selective tracer filtration and retained the absence of collecting ducts and urinary drainage.
change_log.reason: The reported observations support a filtration interpretation without establishing physiological clearance, adult maturity or whole-organ replacement.

change_log.change: Included the 7–8-day nephron-progenitor differentiation result and named cell lines while identifying the stage to which that timing applies.
change_log.reason: Retains useful quantitative manufacturing detail without implying that complete kidneys were produced in that interval.

change_log.change: Separated donor-independent organ supply from possible immune benefits and practical deployment.
change_log.reason: Reduced rejection, freedom from immunosuppression and broad access do not follow automatically from manufacture.

change_log.change: Made acid-base regulation explicit and retained clinical durability, independent manufacture and supply goals as proposed completion criteria.
change_log.reason: Preserves the physiological distinctions in the review without presenting proposed thresholds as established standards.

change_log.change: Preserved visual-review and supplementary-extraction limitations and explained relationships to every other supplied roster entry.
change_log.reason: Makes the evidence boundaries and concept distinctions understandable without implying additional document inspection or merging entries.

unresolved_issues: The supplied record does not establish field-wide progress as of November 1, 2026, or whether the February study was the latest relevant result.
The reported tracer experiments leave comprehensive physiological selectivity, clinically sufficient clearance and adult-organ maturation unresolved.
Collecting-duct formation, integrated urine drainage, therapeutic-scale function and long-term renal replacement remain undemonstrated in the supplied study.
Figures and movies were not visually inspected in the supplied review, and supplementary text extraction could not independently validate image content.
Clinical immune compatibility, rejection risk and any reduction or elimination of immunosuppression require separate evidence.
A future completion protocol must define measurable renal-function, safety, durability, manufacturing and supply endpoints; the supplied sources do not establish numerical acceptance thresholds.

brief.title: Human kidneys grown from cells for transplantation
possible: People with kidney failure could receive a replacement kidney grown from cells and live without dialysis, the treatment that filters blood when kidneys fail. The organ would filter blood, balance water, salts and acidity, and drain urine.
why: Making kidneys through a repeatable production process could create an organ supply independent of living and deceased donors. That could reduce donor shortages and change treatment for people with kidney failure.

sources.who: Murat Tekguc, Takuya Matsumoto and colleagues
sources.showed: They grew kidney organoids, small tissues resembling parts of a kidney, and assembled them into sheets. After implantation in mice, the tissue joined the blood supply and showed filtration that distinguished molecules by size.
sources.quote: Intravital imaging of a nephron sheet implanted in a dorsal skinfold chamber of mice revealed filtration function with size selectability in the organoid glomeruli vascularized with human endothelia.
sources.cited_for: The study supports growing larger amounts of kidney tissue with working blood connections and early filtering function.
sources.not_established: The tissue could not drain urine, and short-term mouse experiments did not establish lasting replacement of kidney function.

sources.who: Min Shi, Kyle W. McCracken and colleagues
sources.showed: They connected nephrons, the kidney’s filtering and processing units, to collecting ducts, the tubes that carry urine onward, within human kidney organoids.
sources.quote: The nephron fusion occurs stereotypically and is regulated by proximal-distal nephron patterning, which can be modulated through temporal manipulation of developmental pathways.
sources.cited_for: The work supports building a connected pathway from filtering tissue into a urine collection system.
sources.not_established: Connected tubes within organoids do not establish urine drainage from a functioning replacement organ.

sources.who: Elena Garreta, Nuria Montserrat and colleagues
sources.showed: They developed a scalable method for producing human kidney organoids. They delivered the organoids into pig kidneys maintained outside the body and detected human cells after transplantation.
sources.quote:
We infuse human kidney organoids into ex vivo porcine kidneys using 
normothermic machine perfusion, and demonstrate in vivo engraftment 
of hPSC-kidney organoids.
sources.cited_for: The work supports repeatable tissue production and delivery into an existing kidney.
sources.not_established: Adding organoids to pig kidneys does not establish manufacture of a complete human replacement kidney.

sources.who: Jeremy J. Song, Harald C. Ott and colleagues
sources.showed: They removed cells from rat kidneys, leaving structural scaffolds, then added new cells. After transplantation into rats, the rebuilt kidneys received blood and produced urine.
sources.quote:
When transplanted in orthotopic position in rat, the grafts were perfused by the recipient’s 
circulation, and produced urine via the ureteral conduit in vivo.
sources.cited_for: The study supports rebuilding kidney structures that connect to blood flow and drain urine.
sources.not_established: The rebuilt rat kidneys remained immature and did not establish durable human kidney replacement.

shown: Researchers have demonstrated separate pieces of the goal in laboratory and animal studies. Tekguc’s team showed early filtering function, Shi’s team connected filtering units to collecting tubes, and Song’s team obtained urine from rebuilt rat kidneys. No study described here demonstrated a manufactured human kidney that could replace a patient’s kidney function.
missing: A complete manufactured human kidney must combine enough mature filtering tissue, dependable blood flow and an exit route for urine.
Transplants must maintain the body’s internal balance safely over the long term.
Manufacturing must reliably control cell types, tissue structure and variation between organs.

milestones.label: Manufactured kidneys sustain patients without dialysis for years
milestones.explanation: Transplants would have to sustain patients for years, with measured filtration, water, salt and acid balance, safe function and reliable urine drainage. This would establish lasting kidney replacement.

milestones.label: Independent teams reproduce organ quality and transplant outcomes
milestones.explanation: Independent teams would have to repeatedly meet defined organ specifications and reproduce transplant outcomes across batches. This would establish how reliably the therapy works under tested conditions.

milestones.label: Practical production offers a path to easing donor shortages
milestones.explanation: Production capacity, failure rates, cost and delivery needs would have to support a credible path to reducing donor scarcity. This would connect clinical success to a useful organ supply.

uncertain: It remains unclear whether early filtering tissue can mature enough to provide the full range of kidney functions.
Whether cell-grown kidneys would reduce rejection or the need for drugs that suppress immunity requires separate clinical evidence.
The standards for sufficient function, safety, durability and production capacity still need definition.

page.title: Bioengineered human kidneys for transplantation
page.definition: A kidney built from human cells would take over enough kidney function after transplantation for the recipient to live without maintenance dialysis. Blood would flow through its nephrons, where glomeruli filter the blood and tubules recover water and dissolved substances the body needs. The remaining fluid would drain as urine. Pig kidney scaffolds repopulated with human cells have filtered blood and produced urine in pigs, but those grafts lacked the tubular cells needed for reabsorption.

goal.need: About 831,000 Americans had kidney failure in 2023. In 2024, the US adult kidney transplant waiting list recorded 3,743 removals because the candidate died. About 90,000 people were waiting for a kidney in October 2026. For someone on in-center hemodialysis, a typical week includes three four-hour treatments. An additional supply of kidneys could shorten the wait for people well enough for transplant surgery and free them from those sessions for as long as the graft works.

completion.title: FDA licenses a human kidney manufactured from cells to replace maintenance dialysis.
completion.criterion: FDA issues a biologics license for a human kidney manufactured from cells, with an approved indication for transplantation to replace maintenance dialysis in people with kidney failure. The evidence establishes safety and effectiveness for that indication, together with manufacturing controls and facilities that ensure continued safety, purity and potency. The cited requirements specify no kidney-specific minimum filtration rate, dialysis-free interval or recipient sample size.
completion.set_by: U.S. Food and Drug Administration, general biologics licensing requirements and CBER biologics license application requirements, applied to the renal-replacement indication.
completion.threshold_quote: FDA approval to market a biologic is granted by issuance of a biologics license.
completion.basis: Licensure evaluates clinical effectiveness for the proposed indication together with the product, manufacturing process and facilities. Applying that existing regulatory test to replacement of maintenance dialysis requires evidence for the intended therapeutic capability. No manufactured kidney appears on FDA’s published list of licensed cellular and gene therapy products.

milestones.title: Implanted kidney tissue receives host blood flow sufficient to sustain cells and physiological function.
milestones.criterion: The implanted kidney tissue recruits host vessels. Blood flow through those vessels sustains the health of the implanted cells and a physiological function of the tissue. The roadmap gives no minimum flow rate or observation period.
milestones.set_by: Kidney Health Initiative, KRT Roadmap, Vascular Access: cellular-based solutions; the target covers implanted cellular products generally.
milestones.threshold_quote: perfusion of implanted tissue that is sufficient to maintain cell health and physiological functions

milestones.title: A manufactured kidney connects filtration and tubular processing to exterior urine drainage.
milestones.criterion: One manufactured kidney filters fluid, passes the filtrate through functioning tubules and discharges the resulting urine through an outlet from the graft. The KidneyX connectivity target gives no minimum urine flow or solute clearance.
milestones.set_by: KidneyX, Artificial Kidney Prize Phase Two announcement, Section B: published component target for artificial kidneys generally.
milestones.threshold_quote: Connectivity for filtration, processing, and exterior drainage of an artificial kidney.

milestones.title: A manufactured kidney functions in an animal with no residual native kidney function.
milestones.criterion: The implanted manufactured kidney demonstrates filtration in an animal with no residual native kidney function. The roadmap leaves the need for the study and its duration to the individual product.
milestones.set_by: Kidney Health Initiative, KRT Roadmap, Blood Filtration: biohybrid solutions; the target covers kidney-replacement technologies generally.
milestones.threshold_quote: function in anephric animal models without residual kidney function

milestones.title: An FDA investigational application permits transplantation of a manufactured human kidney in a trial.
milestones.criterion: An investigational new drug application covering transplantation of the manufactured human kidney goes into effect: 30 days after FDA receives it without a clinical hold, or following earlier FDA notification permitting the investigation to begin. Supporting preclinical studies establish a rationale for use and reasonable safety for the proposed investigation. This is clinical-trial clearance, not marketing approval.
milestones.set_by: U.S. Food and Drug Administration, 21 CFR 312.40 and guidance on early-phase cellular and gene therapy trials; these are general requirements.
milestones.threshold_quote: On earlier notification by FDA that the clinical investigations in the IND may begin.

milestones.title: A first-in-human trial characterizes safety after transplantation of manufactured human kidneys.
milestones.criterion: Recipients receive the manufactured human kidney in an early-phase clinical trial that completes its protocol-defined safety evaluation, including the nature and frequency of adverse reactions and their relationship to dose. FDA also identifies administration feasibility and pharmacological activity as early-phase objectives. The guidance does not prescribe a universal recipient count, observation period or acceptable adverse-event rate.
milestones.set_by: U.S. Food and Drug Administration, Considerations for the Design of Early-Phase Clinical Trials of Cellular and Gene Therapy Products, Section IV.A; general cellular-therapy guidance.
milestones.threshold_quote: the primary objective should be an evaluation of safety

milestones.title: Clinical investigations establish effectiveness of manufactured human kidneys for renal replacement.
milestones.criterion: Clinical investigations of the manufactured human kidney provide substantial evidence of effectiveness for transplantation to replace maintenance dialysis, together with evidence establishing its safety profile in the intended population. The clinical evidence supports the proposed indication in a biologics license application. The cited FDA requirements prescribe no universal kidney-specific numerical success threshold or follow-up duration.
milestones.set_by: U.S. Food and Drug Administration, CBER biologics license application requirements, Clinical Data; a general evidentiary requirement applied to the renal-replacement indication.
milestones.threshold_quote: providing substantial evidence of its effectiveness for the proposed indication.

milestones.title: Engineered kidney tissue performs a measurable kidney function outside the body.
milestones.criterion: Tissue assembled from cells demonstrates a kidney function in a laboratory assay, such as filtration measured by clearance of a solute or tubular reabsorption measured by recovery of glucose from the filtrate. NIDDK specifies a functional tissue target without a minimum clearance or reabsorption fraction.
milestones.set_by: National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases, (Re)Building a Kidney, research objectives for functional tissue generated outside the body
milestones.threshold_quote: Engineer replacement tissue that replicates kidney function.

milestones.title: A manufactured kidney filters blood in a full-scale animal model with residual kidney function.
milestones.criterion: A full-scale animal retains native kidney function after implantation of the manufactured kidney. Measurements attributable to the graft demonstrate blood filtration. The roadmap leaves the need for the study and its duration to the individual product.
milestones.set_by: Kidney Health Initiative, KRT Roadmap, Blood Filtration, mid-term target for biohybrid solutions
milestones.threshold_quote: Demonstrate function in full-scale animal model with residual kidney function

milestones.title: A bioprinted kidney meets PRINT’s pig-model function target with 3–6 months of post-transplant survival.
milestones.criterion: PRINT specifies successful implantation in more than five large animals, 3–6 months of post-transplant survival in a humanized pig model with severe combined immunodeficiency, and assessment at six months for teratomas, rejection and toxicity, all of which must be absent. Its examples of normal function are a glomerular filtration rate of 100–200 mL/min per 70 kg, renal blood flow of 3–5 mL/min per gram and serum creatinine below 2 mg/dL. Teams may justify alternative metrics where these do not fit the product.
milestones.set_by: Advanced Research Projects Agency for Health, PRINT solicitation, Table 2, M3.10 and Phase II deliverable for the bioprinting programme
milestones.threshold_quote: normal organ function in a humanized SCID pig model and survival of 3-6 months post transplantation

not_found: Searches of KidneyX, the KHI roadmap, FDA guidance and EMA cell-based-product guidance found no manufactured-kidney-specific numerical clinical acceptance threshold.
Searches of ClinicalTrials.gov-indexed records found no registered transplantation trial of a whole human kidney manufactured from cells.
Recipient sample size for Song et al.’s rat transplantation experiment was not identified in the accessible main article.
No statement opposing the goal or judging it unachievable was found in the NIDDK, Kidney Health Initiative or ARPA-H programme documents.

results.finding: Human kidney organoids (n = 6) showed greater proximal tubular cation transport in stirred-tank culture than in static culture (p ≤ 0.01).
results.quote: While both static and STR organoids exhibited Rh123 uptake and transport to the lumens of LTL+ tubules, the apical transport of cationic Rh123 from basal sides of tubules was significantly enhanced in STR organoids during the live-cell imaging.

results.finding: Human nephron sheets in NSG mice (6 implantation procedures) showed host perfusion and size-selective filtration during assessments on days 6–11.
results.detail: The paper reports six implantation procedures and does not specify how many individually showed filtration.
results.quote: This observation provided evidence of the successful anastomosis of human organoid vessels with the host’s circulatory system, facilitating the filtration of LMW dextran performed by implanted nephron sheets.

results.finding: Human nephron sheets in mice (6 implantation procedures) showed uptake of 3 kDa dextran by proximal tubules after apparent filtration.
results.detail: The study did not quantify how many implants showed tubular uptake. The authors interpreted tracer localization as evidence consistent with reabsorption.
results.quote: Taken together, both live-cell imaging and fixed tissue analyses suggest that LMW dextran undergoes glomerular filtration and subsequent reabsorption into the interstitial space via tubules.

results.finding: Human nephron sheets in NSG mice (6 implantation procedures) showed graft-localized filtration of circulating 3 kDa dextran.
results.detail: Imaging measured tracer distribution. The study did not report a graft filtration rate or the number of implants that showed filtration.
results.quote: Intravital imaging of a nephron sheet implanted in a dorsal skinfold chamber of mice revealed filtration function with size selectability in the organoid glomeruli vascularized with human endothelia.

results.finding: Human kidney organoid proximal tubules took up 6-carboxyfluorescein after 1 hour in vitro (n unreported).
results.detail: Fluorescence imaging demonstrated tracer uptake. The text describes the uptake qualitatively.
results.quote: they exhibited capacity for robust transport of the organic anion 6-carboxyfluorescein

results.finding: Human kidney organoid grafts had erythrocyte-containing host capillaries at 2 weeks (two grafts per mouse, mouse n unreported).
results.detail: Later duct dilation provided indirect evidence of possible filtration. The recovered fluid volume was too small for biochemical analysis.
results.quote: host-derived endothelial cells (PECAM1) that formed capillaries containing erythrocytes

results.finding: Human kidney organoids averaged 41.8 nephron–collecting duct connections per organoid (quantification n unreported).
results.detail: Collecting ducts formed irregular networks without a common outlet. In transplanted organoids, later duct dilation was consistent with obstruction, and the recovered fluid could not be identified as urine.
results.quote: Quantification of confocal z-stacks showed that organoids contained a mean of 41.8 ± 16.8 (s.d.) epithelial connections between nephron and UB.

results.finding: Perfused recellularized rat kidneys reabsorbed 47.38% of glucose in vitro (sample size unstated).
results.quote: Regenerated kidneys showed partially restored glucose reabsorption of 47.38%, suggesting engraftment of proximal tubular epithelial cells with functional membrane transporters resulting in decreased glucosuria.

results.finding: Implanted recellularized rat kidneys produced 1.2 μL/min of urine under recipient blood flow (sample size unstated).
results.quote: Regenerated kidneys produced urine from shortly after unclamping of recipient vasculature until the planned termination of the experiment.

results.finding: Recellularized rat kidneys reabsorbed 47.38% of glucose and drained urine through the ureter in vitro (sample size unstated).
results.quote: The kidney is perfused via the canulated renal artery (Ra), and renal vein (Rv), while urine is drained via the ureter (U).

results.finding: Rat kidney grafts achieved 0.01 mL/min creatinine clearance after unilateral nephrectomy (sample size unstated).
results.detail: I interpret full-scale as a model at the intended human graft scale. The pig and human kidneys in the supplied text were used for scaffold preparation.
results.quote:
creatinine clearance in regenerated kidneys was lower than that of native kidneys (0.01±0.002 vs. 0.36±0.09 ml min
−1
in controls)

results.finding: Human iPSC kidney organoid grafts (20 glomeruli imaged) showed a median of 40% functional glomeruli per organoid.
results.detail: The median came from tile scans and recorded movies. The 20 glomeruli were the sample for detailed live imaging.
results.quote: we observed that the number of functional glomerular structures had a median of 40% but was variable between organoids

results.finding: Human kidney organoid grafts showed 10 kDa dextran in proximal tubules. The tubular sample size was unreported.
results.detail: The authors interpreted apical tracer localization as evidence of some proximal tubular uptake and endocytosis.
results.quote: This suggests some reuptake and endocytosis of these small dextran molecules in the proximal tubules, thus further corroborating the presence of an active filtration unit.

results.finding: Human kidney organoid grafts in mice showed 10 kDa dextran sieving in 20 imaged glomeruli.
results.detail: The investigators separately observed tracer handling in the underlying native mouse kidney.
results.quote: Glomerular sieving of low molecular mass 10 kDa dextrans could be observed as soon as 1 week after transplantation, and its sieving characteristics did not change thereafter

results.finding: Five human-cell kidney grafts versus five endothelial-only controls showed ex vivo filtration, with lower urine protein and hematocrit than serum (p < 0.0001).
results.quote: Whereas urine protein and HCT values were significantly lower than serum protein and HCT values in bi-culture BEKs, indicating renal filtration.

results.finding: Of five grafts implanted in pigs, the single graft in the final session sustained filtration for up to 5 hours on host blood flow.
results.detail: The study assessed acute graft function using urine and serum measurements.
results.quote: While implant 3 only tested a single BEK, this implant extended the examination window up to 5 hours, demonstrating sustained filtration function with remarkably low (around 1%) urine hematocrit and lower urine protein levels compared to serum protein levels

results.finding: Five grafts in pig implant sessions averaged 1.26 mL/min in ureteral drainage. Grafts in the later sessions showed filtration.
results.detail: The mean includes the first session, which showed no filtration by the reported protein and hematocrit measures.
results.quote: Urine flow rates across the three implant sessions averaged 1.26 mL/min ± 1.3 for values collected at 30 min and 60 min of in vivo perfusion

results.finding: Of five grafts implanted in full-scale pigs, the single graft in the final session produced urine with around 1% hematocrit.
results.detail: The first session showed comparable urine and serum values. Filtration readouts improved in the two later sessions.
results.quote: demonstrating sustained filtration function with remarkably low (around 1%) urine hematocrit and lower urine protein levels compared to serum protein levels

results.finding: Human-cell recellularized rat kidney scaffolds (n = 6) produced 160 ± 8 pg/mL of active vitamin D3 in perfusate.
results.quote:
A signiﬁcantly higher level of 1,
25-dihydroxyvitamin D3 (160 ± 8 pg mL−1) was detected by ELISA in the
treated media compared to the untreated control (Fig. 4d).

results.finding: Human-cell kidney scaffold grafts in NSG mice (n = 6/group) showed host vascular integration and secretory function at 3 weeks.
results.detail: The study assessed perfusion through vascular connections and erythrocyte staining. The criterion sets no minimum flow rate or observation period.
results.quote:
Notably, mouse-graft
vascular anastomosis was evident with erythrocytes present in vasculature and nephron-secreted
proteins detected in mouse urine, indicating functional integration.

results.finding: NSG mice with human-cell kidney scaffold grafts (n = 6/group) had 72.74 ± 13.70 pg/mL of human CD59 in urine.
results.detail: The authors could not visualize a complete nephron extending into a collecting duct. They identified diffusion and active tubular flow as possible routes for the graft proteins detected in host urine.
results.quote:
Thus, the presence of human CD59
and higher level of renin and UMOD in mouse urine indicates that the
engrafted nephrons have function and produce proteins that are excreted
via the lower urinary system of the recipient.

results.finding: Human kidney organoids (n=48 across groups) showed an oxidative phosphorylation phenotype in the smaller-aggregate groups at day 16.
results.detail: The study measured creatinine clearance in whole porcine kidneys during perfusion. It did not attribute that clearance to the infused human organoids.

results.finding: Human kidney organoid-derived cells persisted in porcine kidney autografts through 48 h (n=6 grafts across endpoints).
results.detail: Human DNA and tubular markers were detected in graft biopsies. Fluorescence quantification at the final endpoint was based on one kidney.
results.quote: The results confirm that hPSC-kidney organoids persist at both 24 h and 48 h after kidney reimplantation, albeit a certain degree of damage could be observed in both conditions

results.finding: Pigs with organoid-infused kidney autografts (n=6 across endpoints) had blood creatinine approach baseline at 42 h.
results.detail: The functioning contralateral kidney contributed to the postoperative renal readouts. Creatinine clearance measured during machine perfusion was an ex vivo whole-organ result.
results.quote: Conversely, blood ASAT, urea and creatinine levels peaked at transplantation (Tx) + 18 h and subsequently approached basal levels at Tx + 42 h

results.finding: Human kidney progenitor implants formed masses with perfused glomeruli by 12 weeks in immunodeficient mice (mouse count unreported).
results.quote: By 12 weeks, they formed organ-like masses detectable by bioluminescence imaging. Implants included perfused glomeruli containing human capillaries, podocytes with regions of mature basement membrane, and mesangial cells.

results.finding: Human stem cell-derived nephron implants in immunodeficient mice showed tubular dextran uptake from glomerular filtrate (mouse count and uptake quantity unreported).
results.quote: After intravenous injection of fluorescent low-molecular-weight dextran, signal was detected in tubules, demonstrating uptake from glomerular filtrate.

results.finding: Bioprinted human vascularized proximal tubule tissue (n = 8) reabsorbed approximately 11 μg glucose/mm² at steady state.
results.detail: The authors estimated reabsorbed glucose mass from the concentration difference between channels. Dapagliflozin reduced reabsorption by approximately 98%, and reabsorption gradually recovered after withdrawal.
results.quote: We find that glucose reabsorption increased over time before reaching a steady-state value of ∼11 μg glucose/mm 2  on day 8.

definition = "A kidney built from human cells would take over enough kidney function after transplantation for the recipient to live without maintenance dialysis. Blood would flow through its nephrons, where glomeruli filter the blood and tubules recover water and dissolved substances the body needs. The remaining fluid would drain as urine. Pig kidney scaffolds repopulated with human cells have filtered blood and produced urine in pigs, but those grafts lacked the tubular cells needed for reabsorption.". Reason: The current definition leaves unclear how a graft that produces urine differs from one that can replace dialysis.

goal.need = "About 831,000 Americans had kidney failure in 2023. In 2024, the US adult kidney transplant waiting list recorded 3,743 removals because the candidate died. About 90,000 people were waiting for a kidney in October 2026. For someone on in-center hemodialysis, a typical week includes three four-hour treatments. An additional supply of kidneys could shorten the wait for people well enough for transplant surgery and free them from those sessions for as long as the graft works.". Reason: The current rationale gives prevalence and a funding objective but omits the time patients spend on dialysis, deaths while waiting and the benefit of an additional source of grafts.

add statement by Advanced Research Projects Agency for Health, Personalized Regenerative Immunocompetent Nanotechnology Tissue (PRINT) programme, 2026: "produce immune-matched replacement organs, such as kidneys, hearts, and livers.". Reason: PRINT explicitly names replacement kidneys and distinguishes its programme goal from the narrower objective of its kidney award.

add milestone after None: "Engineered kidney tissue performs a measurable kidney function outside the body.". Reason: The sequence starts after implantation and misses the earlier demonstration that tissue assembled from cells performs a kidney function in the laboratory.

edit m1: criterion = "The implanted kidney tissue recruits host vessels. Blood flow through those vessels sustains the health of the implanted cells and a physiological function of the tissue. The roadmap gives no minimum flow rate or observation period."; refs = [7]. Reason: The mouse experiment and tracer sizes are results from one study, whereas the milestone tests whether host blood flow sustains implanted tissue.

edit m2: criterion = "One manufactured kidney filters fluid, passes the filtrate through functioning tubules and discharges the resulting urine through an outlet from the graft. The KidneyX connectivity target gives no minimum urine flow or solute clearance."; refs = [3]. Reason: The organoid and rat results obscure the requirement that filtration, tubular processing and drainage connect in the same graft.

add milestone after m2: "A manufactured kidney filters blood in a full-scale animal model with residual kidney function.". Reason: The roadmap distinguishes graft function in a full-scale animal with residual kidney function from the later test in an animal with none.

edit m3: criterion = "The implanted manufactured kidney demonstrates filtration in an animal with no residual native kidney function. The roadmap leaves the need for the study and its duration to the individual product."; threshold_quote = "function in anephric animal models without residual kidney function"; threshold_ref = 7; refs = [7]. Reason: The pig organoid-infusion study describes a different intervention and obscures the requirement that the recipient have no residual native kidney function.

add milestone after m3: "A bioprinted kidney meets PRINT’s pig-model function target with 3–6 months of post-transplant survival.". Reason: PRINT supplies a sustained large-animal benchmark for bioprinted kidneys beyond a demonstration of filtration at implantation.
remove not found 3. Reason: The full 2024 OPTN/SRTR report contains the kidney chapter and its table of reasons for adult waiting-list removal.

add not found: "No statement opposing the goal or judging it unachievable was found in the NIDDK, Kidney Health Initiative or ARPA-H programme documents.". Reason: The sources identify technical barriers but leave the question of an institutional objection unanswered.
